blocks.text: Where a founder's day goes, from the research

Most of a founder's day is not building. Asana's index of over 10,000 knowledge workers says 60% of time at work goes to “work about work”. That covers talking about work, searching for information, switching apps and chasing status. Asana's global average is 352 hours a year talking about work, 209 hours on duplicative work and 103 hours in unnecessary meetings. That study covers knowledge workers in general, not founders.

Founder-specific data is thin. The clearest founder number comes from a September 2023 survey of 251 US founders, run by Censuswide for Time Etc. It was reported by StealthAgents, a secondary write-up, so treat it as a strong signal, not a precise measure. It puts admin at 36% of the average founder's work week. On the survey's 45.5-hour week, that is roughly 16 hours.

Interruptions make the gaps worse. Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index surveyed 31,000 knowledge workers in 31 markets. It counts an interruption about every 2 minutes during the 9-to-5 day. Including off-hours, that is 275 a day, based on Microsoft 365 telemetry. The same report says 48% of employees feel their work is chaotic and fragmented.

That is the real problem for a founder. Big blocks, like a hiring plan or a pricing decision, are hard to schedule. The small jobs fill every gap between them. Replies, lookups and logging are the jobs a voice assistant can take off your hands. Start there, not with the strategy work.
Voice assistant for founders on Mac: how it works in an app

Lazur sits in the notch at the top of your Mac screen. Hold ⌥ ⌘, which is Option and Command together, and speak. Lazur reads what is on screen and answers out loud. Ask where something is and it draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Lazur does not click for you. It does not operate Gmail, Slack or Linear on your behalf, and it is not a plugin inside any of them. It works on top of whatever app is open. You never copy the email into a chat window to explain it.

Typing is the other half. Hold fn and dictate, and clean, formatted text lands at your cursor in any app. You can add snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots. Dictation is unlimited on both paid plans.
How an AI assistant for founders drafts your email

Start with the investor reply, since it is the one you think about all day. Open the thread in Gmail in Chrome, or open it in Apple Mail. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and say the decision. Lazur reads the thread on screen and writes the reply into the compose box. Then you read it and send it.

items: Open the thread you want to answer in Gmail or Apple Mail, so the email is on screen.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ and say the decision, for example: “reply, Thursday works, I'll send the deck after”.
Read the draft in the compose box. Check every date, number and name against the thread.
Change one line by hand if the tone is off. Editing is faster than starting from a blank box.
Send it yourself. In Apple Mail, ⇧⌘D sends the message. Lazur does not press Send.

blocks.text: Here is a worked example from a Tuesday. An investor asks whether Thursday works and whether the deck can follow. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and say, “reply, Thursday at 2 Pacific works, deck after the call”. Lazur writes a short reply. You change one word, send it from Mail, and move on. That is less work than typing it from scratch.

Say the decision, not the sentence. “Yes to Tuesday at 10, deck after” gives Lazur what it needs. Long lists of tone rules are rarely needed for a short reply. If the tone is off, say so once and try again.

blocks.title: Name the time zone
blocks.text: Dates and time zones are the easiest part of a reply to get wrong. Say the zone out loud, for example “Thursday at 2 pm Pacific”, so the draft carries it.

Be careful with replies that carry numbers. A valuation, a runway figure or a term clause is yours to check. Lazur reads the screen, and it can misread a figure in a dense table. Open the source row and compare the number before you send.
Research for founders: run it in the background

Research is where a founder's evening often goes. Competitor pricing, a market size or a list of investors can each take an hour of tabs. Say “research our top 5 competitors' pricing” and Lazur starts the job. It runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. You keep working while it runs.

Try a real case. You need pricing for five competitors before a board call. Say, “research our top 5 competitors' pricing, list plan names, monthly price and seat limits in a table.” Finish the deck while the tabs open. When the report arrives, open each pricing page and copy the figures you will say out loud.

Read the summary first. Then open the links in the report and confirm each number. Research output is a starting point. A pricing page can change the same day, and a summary can misstate what a page says.
Give the job a clear shape. Name the companies, the fields and the format. A narrow request gives a usable table. A vague one gives a long essay you have to cut down.
Admin tasks founders can hand off by voice

The same 2023 survey lists the admin tasks founders do each week. Expense logging leads at 59%, then research at 49%, scheduling at 45%, invoicing at 44% and data entry at 43%. Those are the jobs a voice assistant can shorten, one at a time.

Scheduling and research fit a voice assistant well. Expense logging and invoicing need more care. Lazur can explain a sheet, point at a cell and walk you through a menu. It does not operate your accounting app. Dictation can place text at your cursor, but you check every figure yourself.

blocks.text: Capabilities describe how Lazur answers. Explain tells you what is on screen. Point shows where something is. Guide walks you through steps. Draft writes text for you to check. Research runs in the background. Everyday covers calendar, reminders, timers and music. Dictate types at your cursor.
Calendar, reminders and timers by voice on Mac

Say “call with Priya on Friday at 3” and Lazur adds it to your calendar. Say “remind me to send the deck at 9 tomorrow” and it adds a reminder. Timers and music work the same way. You stay in the app you are in.

Calendar has its own keys for the moments you want to see the day. ⌘T goes to today. ⇧⌘T goes to a specific date. ⌘N starts a new event, and ⌘E edits the one you have selected. ⌘, opens Calendar settings. Use the keys to look, and use your voice to add.

Watch the time zone on any event with someone in another city. Say the city in the request, such as “Friday at 3 London time”, so the event lands on the right hour. Check the event in Calendar the first few times you use it.
Keyboard shortcuts founders still need on Mac
Voice does not replace every key. Some jobs are faster with a shortcut. These are the ones to learn first, from Apple's own pages.

items: Mail: ⌘N new message, ⌘R reply, ⇧⌘R reply all, ⇧⌘F forward, ⇧⌘D send.
Spotlight: ⌘Space opens or closes it. ⌘1 to ⌘4 filter to Applications, Files, Actions and Clipboard.
Calendar: ⌘T go to today, ⇧⌘T go to a date, ⌘N new event, ⌘E edit event, ⌘, settings.
Lazur: hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about the screen, and hold fn to dictate.

blocks.text: Apple says shortcuts vary by language and keyboard layout. If a key does nothing, check your input source in System Settings. Mail's search shortcut is not on Apple's page, so use the search field in the Mail window instead.
What leaves your Mac and what stays there

Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. When it answers, the audio and a screenshot go to AI providers. Those are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Memory of what you asked and did is kept on the Mac.

That is not the same as a rule for your company's data. An investor thread can hold terms you agreed to keep private. A support inbox can hold customer records. Follow your company's rules, your NDAs and your contracts before you ask Lazur to read that screen.
If you are not sure, ask your lawyer or your co-founder first. A quick check now costs less than an apology later.
Mistakes founders make with an AI assistant

items: Sending a draft without reading it. Lazur writes what it reads. A wrong name or date still goes out under your name.
Trusting a research table without opening the pages. Prices change. Open each source and compare.
Asking a short question and expecting a long answer. Ask one thing, get one usable answer, then ask the next.
Expecting clicks. Lazur points, explains and guides. You click.
Pasting private customer or investor data without a check. Follow your company's rules first.
Starting the trial in a quiet week. The 3-day trial starts when you first open the app, so open it when your inbox is busy.

blocks.text: Most of these come from one habit. People treat a voice assistant as a worker that finishes the job. Treat it as a fast colleague who reads, drafts and points. You still finish the job.
How to start with Lazur as a founder this week

items: Download Lazur for Mac from the [download page](/download). It runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
Open the app. The 3-day Pro trial starts then, with no credit card.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ on a real email thread and ask for one reply. Check it before you send.
Run one research job on a list you already need, such as competitor pricing. Compare the output with the pages.
Add one calendar event and one reminder by voice. Check both in Calendar.

blocks.text: After the 3-day trial, Pro costs $18 a month, or $15 a month billed annually, and includes 250 AI actions. Power costs $120 a month, or $96 a month billed annually, and includes 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both. Check the [pricing page](/pricing) before you choose.

Pick Pro if your week is mostly email, calendar and a few research jobs. Pick Power if you run research most days. Count your AI actions for one week before you decide, so the choice rests on your own use.

blocks.title: Before you paste data
blocks.text: Confidential investor terms, customer records and health or payment data need a check first. This page does not claim any compliance certification. Follow your company's rules before you share that screen.

Start small. Pick one reply, one research job and one reminder this week. Then decide whether the time you save is worth the price. faq.question: Can Lazur send emails for me?
faq.answer: No. It writes the draft into the compose box at your cursor. You read it and send it yourself. In Apple Mail, ⇧⌘D sends the message.

faq.question: Does Lazur work in every app?
faq.answer: It works on top of any Mac app that is open, including Gmail, Slack, Notion, Google Sheets, Linear and Chrome. It explains, points and guides. It does not operate those apps for you.

faq.question: Is it always listening?
faq.answer: No. Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold ⌥ ⌘. The audio and screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored.

faq.question: How long is the free trial?
faq.answer: There is a 3-day Pro trial with no credit card. It starts when you first open the app, so plan to open it during a busy week.

faq.question: How many AI actions do I get?
faq.answer: Pro includes 250 AI actions and Power includes 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both plans. Check the pricing page for the current terms before you buy.

faq.question: Does Lazur run on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur is for macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.
